architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: For both independent repeats, SI_15_60 must be below 3.80%. This is below half of the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% for reactive mass fraction 0.8000 and supports formulation-level superlinear suppression relative to H-CORE.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: The selected candidate is marked modified_chemistry_unvalidated because AC1920 and TK100 are outside the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI shared-shape support. However, SI_15_60 is read directly by the 120 C thermal hold and does not depend on transferring that shared rheological regularity; therefore the direct formulation-level drift result is admissible, but it cannot establish broader modified-chemistry shape transfer or a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If both independent repeats have SI_15_60 at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result is consistent with H-CORE linear dilution. If both repeats are below 3.80%, H-CORE is falsified at the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution. Results with one repeat in each region, or with either repeat between 3.80% and 7.61%, are non-separating rather than falsifying; H-RESIN and H-DUAL remain mutually unresolved because both modifier axes are active.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run the corresponding acrylic-only M-HOLD-120 condition at 15% AC1920 and 0% TK100, with the same preparation history and repeat rule, to test whether suppression requires the minor tackifier-like axis and to distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured at 120 C over 15-60 minutes
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41 is the minimum-burden supported dual-axis intervention that directly tests whether 120 C viscosity drift is substantially below the 7.61% linear-dilution benchmark. It is intended to mitigate the observed hot-hold failure while distinguishing reactive-core dilution from a combined suppression alternative. The result will be interpreted strictly as a formulation-level rheological outcome, not as evidence for a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator in selecting S1C41::M-HOLD-120 because it is in the deterministic tied top set, directly measures the declared failure mode, and uses the smallest supported dual-axis modifier burden. I followed the Skeptic's correction that the experiment cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL or establish axis-specific causation. The advisory chemistry audit is not ignored: the modified chemistry is scientifically acceptable here only because the selected measurement observes drift directly rather than using an unsupported shared-shape transfer.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: The candidate lies within the externally supported coarse AC1920 and TK100 regions, but the combined dual-axis effect and modifier functionality are not locally verified; the 0.8000 reactive-mass benchmark requires verified stoichiometric validity.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Low for the directly measured 120 C, 15-60 minute drift window, but high for transferring the result to other temperatures, formulations, shared-shape models, or molecular explanations.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: M-HOLD-120 directly calculates SI_15_60 from viscosity at 15 and 60 minutes without fitting or extrapolation; the declared discrimination threshold is 2.00 percentage points, with at least two independent repeats required.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: Moderate-to-high because M-HOLD-120 does not control process state; preparation history must be matched and recorded, and discordant repeats should be treated as non-separating.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local rheological regularities were measured in the original reactive polyurethane hot-melt formulation family anchored by E2, with E1/E2/E3 same-system temperature sweeps and a separate E1 +P chemical-perturbation check. The intended experiment should remain inside this chemistry family; if a chemistry-changing modifier such as AC1920 or TK100 is introduced, transfer of the local regularities is not assumed without an applicability check.
planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence (thermal-hold drift)
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original 120 C matched-window hold shows SI_15_60 of 51.54% for E5, compared with 9.51% for the least-drifting original reference E1.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Only two original formulations have thermal-hold measurements, each with four time points over 15-90 minutes, and the observed SI values are widely separated (9.51% for E1 versus 51.54% for E5). This provides evidence of a failure but does not resolve the trajectory across the candidate modifier axes or distinguish dilution from superlinear suppression and tackifier dependence.
measurement_requirements: Perform a matched-window 120 C thermal hold with viscosity recorded at 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes and report SI_15_60 directly.
Use at least two independent repeats with the same documented preparation and thermal history so the drift difference can be compared with the 2 percentage-point discrimination threshold.

Measure candidate compositions with known reactive mass fraction and modifier-axis composition, including an acrylic-like-only condition and a condition with a nonzero minor tackifier when those are being compared.
Retain the full time trajectories, not only a fitted descriptor, so linear-dilution behavior can be distinguished from superlinear suppression within the measured 15-60 minute window.
planner.scientific_question: For a candidate in the local reactive polyurethane formulation family, is its 120 C matched-window viscosity drift consistent with reactive-core linear dilution, or is it substantially suppressed by resin modification; if suppression occurs, does it require a nonzero minor tackifier axis rather than acrylic-like modification alone?

planner_action_requests_after_forcing.name: query_external_priors
planner_action_requests_after_forcing.reason: Local hold coverage is sparse, so source-level analogue evidence is needed to assess whether the proposed modifier-axis comparison remains within a defensible chemistry boundary.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: The candidate chemistry is outside the validated unmodified chemistry family for shared thermal-shape transfer, so shape-based M-ANCHOR inference would be unsupported. However, M-HOLD-120 reads thermal-hold drift directly without using that regularity and is therefore scientifically admissible. The 15% acrylic-like and 5% minor-tackifier-like levels lie within the externally supported intervention regions.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If matched 15-60 minute drift remains below 3.80% across at least two repeats, the result supports H-RESIN over H-CORE and indicates suppression substantially stronger than the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction. Because both modifier axes are active, it does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If drift is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result is consistent with H-CORE's linear-dilution prediction. If drift is below 3.80%, H-CORE is falsified at the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A drift between 3.80% and 7.61%, or a result too variable across repeats to resolve the 2.00 percentage-point threshold, leaves H-CORE and H-RESIN unresolved. A subsequent acrylic-only hold would be required to distinguish resin suppression from the tackifier-dependent H-DUAL mechanism.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Deterministically tied, but uses 17.5% acrylic-like modifier and therefore a larger departure and modifier burden than S1C41 without increasing hypothesis discrimination.
Deterministically tied, but uses 20% acrylic-like modifier and a larger perturbation than the minimum sufficient 15% level.
Deterministically tied, but uses 22.5% acrylic-like modifier and thus a larger justified departure from the local reactive-core chemistry.
Deterministically tied, but uses the maximum 25% acrylic-like modifier, increasing intervention burden without improving direct discrimination.
Lower VOI because its 2.5% tackifier-like level is outside the repeatedly documented 4.8-6.4% cluster and incurs greater extrapolation risk.

proposer.reasoning: The failure mode is directly measured isothermal drift, so M-HOLD-120 is preferable to model-dependent M-ANCHOR or M-SWEEP. S1C41 separates the reactive-core prediction from both suppression-related alternatives, stays within the supported modifier regions, and is the least burdensome member of the genuinely tied top set. Its direct observable remains admissible despite the absence of validated shared-shape transfer in the modified chemistry.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have identical VOI component vectors and are genuinely tied. S1C41 uses the smallest total modifier burden among the tied set while remaining inside both supported regions: 15% acrylic-like modifier is the conservative lower supported band and 5% minor tackifier-like modifier is in the repeatedly documented minor-resin cluster. It therefore minimizes departure from the characterized reactive core while directly testing the same hypothesis contrasts.

residual_decision_risk: The dual-axis intervention confounds acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like effects.
The reactive-mass dilution benchmark requires verified modifier functionality and stoichiometric correction; otherwise the 7.61% benchmark may be invalid.
M-HOLD-120 does not control process state, and the protocol lacks a predefined repeat-aggregation or discordance rule.
The experiment supports a formulation-level drift pattern, not the molecular encounter-frequency mechanism proposed within H-RESIN.

The modified AC1920/TK100 chemistry is outside validated shared-shape support; direct drift remains admissible, but unmodified-family shape transfer, M-ANCHOR use, and broader modified-chemistry generalization remain unsupported.
An intermediate or variable result may leave H-CORE versus suppression unresolved.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is valid: S1C41 changes both modifier axes, so its M-HOLD-120 result can distinguish H-CORE from a combined suppression alternative but cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL or attribute suppression to either axis. This does not change which experiment should be run for the stated performance-mitigation objective, because the proposal explicitly declares that pair unresolved and the direct 120 C drift observable remains informative. It changes the interpretation and prevents claims of full three-hypothesis discrimination or axis-specific causation. The tie does not itself require replacing S1C41: all tied cards have identical VOI component vectors, and S1C41 is the minimum-burden supported member. A separate acrylic-only hold would be needed if causal axis isolation became the primary objective.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposal is in the five-card tied top set. No re-weighting in the reported 25-scenario sweep changed the tied top set: top_experiment_set_stability was 1.0, intervention-family and measurement-plan stability were both 1.0, and every recommendation_flip_boundary survived the entire sweep. The base margin to the first strictly lower experiment was 0.004583. These perturbations are defensible as sensitivity tests of the transparent VOI weighting, but the stability is decision stability rather than confidence or evidence that the experiment is scientifically correct. Within the tie, S1C41 is scientifically preferred because it uses the smallest supported dual-axis modifier burden while retaining direct drift measurement.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary observable SI_15_60 remains inside the measurement support because M-HOLD-120 reads 120 C time-dependent drift directly and does not reuse the unmodified-family shared thermal-response shape. Nevertheless, S1C41 is modified_chemistry_unvalidated; any shared-shape or broader modified-chemistry transfer claim would require a direct M-SWEEP on the modified composition before using M-ANCHOR or asserting shape transfer.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The protocol directly measures the required 15-60 minute drift at 120 C, and the S1C41 thresholds of 3.80% and 7.61% are separated by 3.81 percentage points, exceeding the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution. Thus results consistently below 3.80% or at/above 7.61% across the required repeats are attainable. The protocol should still predefine repeat aggregation and process-history controls because M-HOLD-120 does not control process state.
leakage_findings: No unmeasured outcome or validation-formulation identity is explicitly used in the stated rationale; the payload says the recommendation was outcome-blind.
The planned rheological hold cannot establish the molecular encounter-frequency mechanism stated within H-RESIN; it can only test the formulation-level drift prediction.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low-drift result cannot be claimed to establish resin-wide superlinear suppression rather than tackifier-dependent suppression; only H-CORE versus a combined suppression alternative is supported.
objections.objection: The selected S1C41::M-HOLD-120 composition predicts 3.804% drift for both H-RESIN and H-DUAL, while H-CORE predicts 7.608%. Thus the experiment separates H-CORE from the two suppression hypotheses by more than the declared 2.00 percentage-point resolution, but cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL. The proposer correctly lists this pair under hypotheses_not_separated, but inconsistently lists H-DUAL under hypotheses_separated and says the experiment separates all three.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The result cannot attribute suppression to the minor tackifier axis, cannot test whether acrylic-only material remains near the linear-dilution prediction, and cannot adjudicate the mechanistic specialization asserted by H-DUAL.
objections.objection: S1C41 changes both modifier axes simultaneously: AC1920 is 15.0 wt% and TK100 is 5.0 wt%, while reactive mass fraction is changed to 0.8000. The matched-window drift is therefore jointly attributable to acrylic-like modification, minor tackifier-like modification, and reactive-core dilution. No acrylic-only condition is included in the selected protocol.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A deviation from 7.61% could reflect an incorrect dilution baseline or stoichiometry rather than superlinear resin suppression, weakening both H-CORE falsification and H-RESIN support.
objections.objection: The H-CORE benchmark of 7.61% is computed as E1_drift 9.51% multiplied by reactive mass fraction 0.8000. That benchmark assumes AC1920 and TK100 are chemically inert and that their normalized total-weight fractions map directly to reaction-capable mass fraction. The payload explicitly notes that reactive OH or other NCO-reactive groups require recalculation, but S1C41 has no verified modifier functionality or stoichiometric correction in the experiment protocol.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The primary drift quantity remains interpretable, but inconsistent treatment of the two repeats could make borderline classification non-reproducible.
objections.objection: The primary observable SI_15_60 is directly calculated from viscosity at 15 and 60 minutes under M-HOLD-120, with no fit, extrapolation, or imputation. This attack surface largely survives. However, the protocol also records 30 and 45 minute points without specifying how repeat-level variability or disagreement between repeats will be summarized for the criterion.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A direct low-drift result could support the observed S1C41 formulation-process point, but not a validated shared-shape claim for AC1920/TK100 compositions.
objections.objection: The direct M-HOLD-120 observable does not reuse the shared thermal-response shape and is therefore not invalidated by the unmodified-family support boundary. However, S1C41 is explicitly marked modified_chemistry_unvalidated, with shared_shape_use set to verification_only and no prior verified shape transfer. The experiment can measure drift in the modified chemistry, but it cannot transfer the unmodified-family thermal regularity or generalize the result to modified-composition behavior beyond this direct hold.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The criterion can be met by the measurement, but a variable preparation history or discordant repeats may leave the classification indeterminate even when the nominal mean appears to cross a threshold.
objections.objection: The numerical separation is attainable in principle: the H-CORE threshold is 3.80%, the H-RESIN falsification threshold is 7.61%, and the gap exceeds the declared 2.00% resolution. However, M-HOLD-120 has controls_process_state set to false, a process_state_risk score of 0.75, six missing process fields, and only the minimum two repeats. The payload does not define a repeat-aggregation or variance rule for deciding whether the result is consistently below 3.80% or at/above 7.61%.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment's result could be overinterpreted as confirming a molecular mechanism when it only discriminates observed drift relative to an empirical dilution benchmark.
objections.objection: M-HOLD-120 can establish a formulation-level rheological drift pattern, but it cannot establish the molecular explanation in H-RESIN that suppression occurs through lowered effective concentration and reaction-capable-species encounter frequency. The payload's claim boundary explicitly excludes molecularly resolved reaction pathways and identifies E_eta as rheological rather than molecular.

skeptic.recommended_change: Add an acrylic-only M-HOLD-120 condition at the same 15% AC1920 level with zero TK100, alongside the selected dual-axis condition, and preverify modifier reactive functionality so the 0.8000 reactive-mass dilution benchmark is chemically valid. Use identical preparation history and a predefined repeat-level classification rule.
skeptic.strongest_objection: S1C41::M-HOLD-120 activates AC1920 and TK100 together, so its direct drift result cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL or attribute suppression to either modifier axis. The experiment therefore cannot deliver the full three-hypothesis discrimination implied by the VOI ranking and the hypotheses_separated field.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_GJJ_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 GJJ day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

result.source_scope: original pre-validation local measurements with chemistry-comparability audit

tool_trace.reason: Retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis and modifier-axis structure needed to select a candidate that can distinguish reactive-core, resin-modification, and dual-axis mechanisms.

evidence: PAT_US20160215185A1: repeated acrylic tackifying resin examples at approximately 19-20% of total formulation
PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

args.candidate_space_role: acrylic-like and minor tackifier-like modifier axes

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is ADVISORY. Every experiment card above remains selectable, including the cards the audit marks inadmissible. Use the audit as scientific evidence and justify whatever you select.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.admissibility_reason: The matched-window 120 C hold observes thermal-hold drift directly and does not reuse the shared thermal-response shape, so it stays admissible outside the validated chemistry family.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.
